lf-playground.description: A reusable interactive playground that coordinates one JSON-safe working configuration, one operable preview, one displayed instruction, and one final `choose` action. Put it inside lf-ask when the configuration is a question for the user. Direct children are controls, presets, one preview, and one output. Built-in controls contribute scalar fields; a page module registers structured contributors through `registerContributor(name, defaultSnapshot, {read, apply})` and calls the returned notifier after its gestures. One optional `registerInstructionProvider(values => text)` derives the displayed instruction. Restore, reset, copy, projection, change events, and submission all use the same aggregate values. The page's complete lf-playground declaration gives task-specific values their exact action schema.

lf-playground-control.description: One typed input in a playground. `name` is the stable key in the submitted value map and in the reflected CSS property and data attribute. `label` names the generated control. Every kind declares its initial value as a string: a finite number for range, `true` or `false` for toggle, one child value for choice, a six-digit hex colour for color, and arbitrary text for text. Range controls must add max and may add min, step, and unit. Choice controls contain one or more lf-playground-choice children; other kinds are empty.

lf-playground-choice.description: One labeled value in a choice control. The value is stored and reflected; the label is the control text shown to the user.

lf-playground-preset.description: One named partial configuration. Activating the generated preset button applies each child setting and leaves controls not named by the preset unchanged. The button remains visibly selected while all of its settings match the current values.

lf-playground-setting.description: One value applied by a playground preset. `for` names a control in the same playground and `value` uses that control's authored string form.

lf-playground-preview.description: The real, operable artifact a playground previews. An A/B comparison mounts both candidates here; `leaf page guidance <page> author` says how one state drives them. Page CSS may bind reflected values from the enclosing lf-playground. An inline page module may consume the playground's public values and change event, own gestures and computed state, and load vendored or page-media assets from the page's origin.

lf-playground-output.description: The natural-language instruction produced by a playground. Write a self-contained task rather than a value dump, and place lf-playground-value elements where selected scalar values make the task more precise. A page module may instead register one instruction provider when structured or conditional values determine the prose. The choose action sends the exact displayed instruction beside the complete typed value map. The package keeps this output live and offers a copy button.

lf-playground-value.description: One live value inside a playground instruction. `for` names a control in the enclosing playground. Numeric values include the control's unit.
